text:
Predicates:
Engaged(x) ::: x is engaged.
WeddingPlans(x) ::: x makes wedding plans.
Invite(x, y) ::: x invites y to their ceremony.
Wedding(x) ::: x has a wedding.
WellAttended(x) ::: x has a well-attended wedding.
LargerFamily(x) ::: x has a larger family.
John ::: John.

Premises:
∀x (WeddingPlans(x) → Engaged(x)) ::: All people who make wedding plans are engaged.
∀x (Invite(x, y) → WeddingPlans(x)) ::: All people who invite others make wedding plans.
∀x (WellAttended(x) → Invite(x, y)) ::: Anyone with a well-attended wedding invites others.
∀x (LargerFamily(x) → (Wedding(x) ∨ Invite(x, y))) ::: People with larger families have a wedding or invite to their ceremony.
Engaged(John) → ¬Invite(John, y) ∧ WeddingPlans(John) ::: If John is engaged, then John does not invite friends and makes wedding plans.
LargerFamily(John) → (Wedding(John) ∨ Invite(John, y)) ::: If John has a larger family, then John has a well-attended wedding or invites friends.

Conclusion:
¬LargerFamily(John) ::: John does not have a larger family.
